newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Ferrell FX Index up 4.9 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Ferrell FX Index up 4.9 pct in October.

text.p: The Ferrell FX Index rose 4.9 percent in October with the median return up 2.3 percent, Ferrell Capital Management said on Monday.
Thirty-one of 35 programs reported positive results in October, Ferrell said.
Friedberg Commodity Management Inc, of Toronto, once again turned in the month's top performace, reporting gains of 18.8 percent. Friedberg placed first in September, as well.

"Strong economic data out of the United Kingdom and ... expectations of a hike in interest rates pushed sterling to new highs against the dollar and mark," Friedberg vice president Rick Zauderer told Ferrell.
Baltimore-based Campbell & Co placed second in October, gaining 16.5 percent, Ferrell said. And New York-based Tamiso & Co came in third, reporting gains of 11.7 percent.
"In October, sterling appreciated five percent, there was a 2.5 percent weakening in the yen and the mark exhibited increased volatility," said Ferrell president William Ferrell.
"As the debate rages over the timing of the European Monetary Union, traders continue to expand their market coverage to the secondary currencies," he added.
For the 118-month period from January 1987 through October 1996, the compounded annual return of the Ferrell FX Index is 17.8 percent.

The index provides a benchmark for multi-advisor currency portfolios and includes 35 programs managed by 32 firms located in the United States, United Kingdom, France, Canada, Ireland and Switzerland.
